title: From The River To The Sea, Our People Will Be Free

sense.text:
The scholars themselves bring out that Christ was a black Israelite from Galilee, so the Sanhedrin, the court in Jerusalem that tried and condemned him, was a black court too: black Jews in Jerusalem, black scribes and black Pharisees, collaborating with the white Roman oppressor to keep their political and social privileges, just like they do today. Pilate and Herod were the white ones.

“Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.” They had their allegiance to the Roman Empire. The black Sanhedrin had their allegiance to Rome, just like the black Christian church today has its allegiance to America, which is an extension of Rome.

“Also Edom shall be a desolation: every one that goeth by it shall be astonished, and shall hiss at all the plagues thereof. As in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighbour cities thereof”. When it talks about Edom here, going down like Sodom and Gomorrah, that is talking about America, Babylon the great: “no man shall abide there, neither shall a son of man dwell in it.”

“Behold, he shall come up like a lion from the swelling of Jordan”: the he there is the United States of America. The swelling of Jordan is when Jordan overflows its banks, and that is the first month; so the time this comes is the first month. On the map the Jordan River runs down the center, between the West Bank and the actual Jordan, with Jordan to the right and the West Bank and Israel to the left.

“But I will suddenly make him run away from her”: the Lord will suddenly do it, and the her here is NATO. “Who will appoint me the time?” Who is going to tell the Lord when to do it?

“Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord, that he hath taken against Edom”: write it down, Edom here is NATO. “And his purposes, that he hath purposed against the inhabitants of Teman”: Teman is America, the USA. That is who it makes reference to.

“Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out”: that is so-called Israel. On the map the green is the Arab world and that tiny speck is Israel, the least of the flock, the smallest one there, surrounded by other heathen nations. Surely Israel shall draw out America.

“Surely he shall make their habitations desolate”: there is going to be war, and something is going to happen to America. Their habitations are going to be destroyed; she is going to fall.

“The earth is moved at the noise of their fall”: the earth is going to be moved at the noise of America’s fall. “At the cry the noise thereof was heard in the Red sea”: the people in the Red Sea are going to hear the destruction of the United States of America. Everybody is going to hear it. It is the same thing the prophet Joel spoke of in Joel 2.

“Behold, he shall come up and fly as the eagle”: that is the United States of America, put up their famous jet planes. America is coming to the rescue; the northern army is coming to rescue Israel. “And spread his wings over Bozrah”: on the map Bozrah sits in what they call Jordan, that whole beige area is Jordan, and Bozrah is right there.

“And at that day shall the heart of the mighty men of Edom be as the heart of a woman in her pangs”: they are going to be afraid, because NATO is going to turn against them.

“Concerning Damascus”: write it down, Damascus is Syria, modern day Syria. “Hamath is confounded”: Hamath is one of the cities of Syria. “For they have heard evil tidings: they are fainthearted; there is sorrow on the sea”: when that devastation happens to America, everybody is going to hear about it. “It cannot be quiet”: you can’t hide this thing.

“Damascus is waxed feeble, and turneth herself to flee”: Damascus is going to run during this time. “Anguish and sorrows have taken her, as a woman in travail.” Why is Syria going to be sad over America? Because America makes a lot of nations wealthy. You might say America has no dealings with Syria; that’s not true. America always hands out money, making these countries wealthy. That is what Revelation 18 shows: the kings and the merchants of the earth bewail her.
“How is the city of praise not left, the city of my joy!” Not left from being destroyed. The city of praise, the city of my joy, is talking about Israel, as Jeremiah 33 shows.

“Therefore her young men shall fall in her streets”: the young men in Israel shall fall in the streets. That is talking about Amalek over there. “And all the men of war shall be cut off in that day, saith the Lord of hosts.”

precepts.why: “And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.” Babylon goes down like Sodom and Gomorrah, and Jeremiah 49 says Edom shall be a desolation “As in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah”. That shows that when it talks about Edom here it is talking about America, Babylon the great.

To get understanding of what it means when it says the swelling of Jordan. “And as they that bare the ark were come unto Jordan, and the feet of the priests that bare the ark were dipped in the brim of the water, (for Jordan overfloweth all his banks all the time of harvest,) That the waters which came down from above stood and rose up”. The swelling of Jordan is Jordan overflowing all his banks, and that is all the time of harvest.

“The waters of Jordan returned unto their place, and flowed over all his banks, as they did before. And the people came up out of Jordan on the tenth day of the first month”. So when did the Jordan overflow? The first month, not the tenth month: the tenth is the day.

“These are they that went over Jordan in the first month, when it had overflown all his banks; and they put to flight all them of the valleys, both toward the east, and toward the west.” Again, what month did the Jordan overflow its banks? The first month. So when Jeremiah 49 says “he shall come up like a lion from the swelling of Jordan”, the month this is going to be is the first month.

When Jeremiah says “at the cry the noise thereof was heard in the Red sea”, it is the same thing the prophet Joel talked about. Repetition leads to mastery.

“Let the priests, the ministers of the Lord, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare thy people”. Why must they say that? Because there is going to be an onslaught against our people, which is what we read in the book by Tony Martin about the ADL, the Jewish onslaught against black people. It is really against the twelve tribes of Israel; any inkling of us waking up to our identity is detrimental to them. They are creating cop city in Atlanta, where they train all law enforcement throughout the country how to deal with civil unrest and uprisings, and really it is to be against the twelve tribes of Israel and this teaching. Tribulation is going to be against our people because of the teachings of the Holy Bible, that we’re the Jews and they are not. They hate that; our repenting leads to their destruction, and they don’t want it taught. This is war.

“Give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?” They are going to make mockery as they are killing and imprisoning a certain remnant of us: these Israelites said they’re the children of God; you’re in jail now, you got no food, you got no water, we whipped you, we urinated on you, where’s your God now?

“Then will the Lord be jealous for his land, and pity his people”: his land is on one side of the earth and his people on this side of the earth. “I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen: But I will remove far off from you the northern army”. That is the part we wanted to get to: he is going to cause something to happen in the Middle East. “And will drive him into a land barren and desolate”: that land is the land of Israel. “With his face toward the east sea”: the east sea is the Dead Sea. “And his hinder part toward the utmost sea”: the utmost sea is the Mediterranean, to the left on the map. “And his stink shall come up, and his ill savour shall come up, because he hath done great things”: they are going to be destroyed.

Back in Jeremiah 49, the eagle that comes up is the United States of America: the northern army coming to rescue Israel.

Why is Syria going to be sad? “And the kings of the earth, who have committed fornication and lived deliciously with her, shall bewail her, and lament for her, when they shall see the smoke of her burning”. Some of these are the same ones that are going to destroy her, America. “Standing afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come.”

“And the merchants of the earth”, the corporations of the earth, “shall weep and mourn over her; for no man buyeth their merchandise any more”. America makes a lot of nations wealthy. You might say America has no dealings with Syria, but that’s not true: America always hands out money, making these countries wealthy.

To explain the city of praise, the city of my joy. “And it shall be to me a name of joy, a praise and an honour before all the nations of the earth, which shall hear all the good that I do unto them”. Start at verse 7 to know what it is talking about: “And I will cause the captivity of Judah and the captivity of Israel to return, and will build them, as at the first. And I will cleanse them from all their iniquity”. So now we know the city of praise in Jeremiah 49:25 is talking about Israel.

sense.text: As we watched the tunnels, Job kept popping up in mind. “They were driven forth from among men, (they cried after them as after a thief;)”: we chased them like they were thieves, like they stole something.

“To dwell in the clifts of the valleys, in caves of the earth, and in the rocks.” They are always known for digging. Just like they dug those caves out: all that is man-made digs that they did during the Middle Ages. That is what Amalek did.

“They were children of fools, yea, children of base men”: base men, add the T and you’ve got basement. It’s the lowest of the low; God says they are the lowest. “They were viler than the earth”: God says they are viler than the earth.
“And now am I their song, yea, I am their byword.” Now they talk about us being the vilest thing, but God says they are the vilest thing. They make us their byword.

We often read this in the context of our people, but the proper context, for you teachers out there, is Esau, the so-called white man; it’s going to explain itself.

“They are of those that rebel against the light; they know not the ways thereof”: they know not the ways of God. That’s why they’ll read the Talmud before they read the Torah. “Nor abide in the paths thereof”: they do not abide in the paths of God’s laws.
“The murderer rising with the light killeth the poor and needy”, and the poor is Zion, our people (Isaiah 14:32). “And in the night is as a thief.”

“The eye also of the adulterer waiteth for the twilight”: they are the true adulterers that wait for the twilight. “Saying, No eye shall see me: and disguiseth his face.” Look at the Boston Tea Party: white folks dressed up as the so-called Native American Indians. They disguise themselves; they often do that.

“In the dark they dig through houses, which they had marked for themselves in the daytime: they know not the light.” That is what we just found out: they dug tunnels to four adjoining buildings, tunnels 60 feet long and 8 feet across. They find buildings that they like and they dig tunnels to them.

“For the morning is to them even as the shadow of death”: once you find out who they are, you find out that God hates this group of people, this race. “If one know them, they are in the terrors of the shadow of death.”

That’s why Tony Martin in his book shows that once you discover who these people are, you become number one enemy to them. This is why no entertainer speaks up against them, and why the police department deals with them with … gloves: throwing wood at the police, popping them upside the head, and nothing happens to them.

precepts.why:
To explain the poor, for the new people online: “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.” Zion, the poor of his people.

So when the Bible talks about the poor, it’s talking about Zion, the people of Israel, our people. The murderer rising with the light is Esau killing our people.

sense.text: “I saw the Lord standing upon the altar: and he said, Smite the lintel of the door, that the posts may shake”: he is prophesying the destruction of the temple of Jerusalem, 70 AD. “He that fleeth of them shall not flee away, and he that escapeth of them shall not be delivered.” So Israel was destroyed in 70 AD. Now read on for what happens regarding Rome.

“Though they dig into hell, thence shall mine hand take them; though they climb up to heaven, thence will I bring them down.” For what the white men did to our people, there is no place they are going to be able to hide. Whether they dig into hell or go up into space, God said there is no place they can hide that he will not find them.

“And though they hide themselves in the top of Carmel, I will search and take them out thence.” “And though they be hid from my sight in the bottom of the sea”: what goes down to the bottom of the sea? That isn’t talking about our people. This is Esau going to the bottom of the sea in their submarines, and God will “command the serpent, and he shall bite them.”

Prophecy is a good thing, and we love prophecy. But Paul prays “that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give unto you the spirit of wisdom”: brothers, we all want God to give us the spirit of wisdom. “And revelation”: we want the Lord to bless us with that spirit of revelation, “in the knowledge of him.” That’s what you pray for; if y’all ain’t praying for it, you better pray for it.

‘The Bible is the most valuable treasure of knowledge, but it is applying God’s laws that turns that knowledge into wisdom.’

“The eyes of your understanding being enlightened”: brothers, understand that. “That ye may know what is the hope of his calling”: y’all are called in here for a reason. It’s not just to get a wife or a spouse. It’s to improve our lives and gear ourselves towards getting the kingdom of heaven on earth, to gather the twelve tribes of Israel. “And what the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints.”

precepts.why:
“Open thou mine eyes”: this is what David said, and this is what we ought to say. It’s talking about our spiritual eyes, not the eyes y’all got in your head; it’s your mental eye, what the world calls your third eye. That is the eyes of your understanding being enlightened.

“That I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.” That’s why we say four chapters a day, and read consistently. What you see today you didn’t see yesterday. There are things read over and over and over again and not seen until last week, like, oh shoot, look at this. The Lord has to open up your spiritual eye, and it comes through constant reading.

sense.text:
Now we’re going to talk about a carpenter. Write this down: a carpenter is a builder. Prophecy is good, but without us being builders in his truth it’s all pointless; we’re just going to die in a devastation just like our enemies, and we don’t want that. A carpenter in the Bible is a learned man, and a learned man is able to build broken spirits.

“How long wilt thou not have mercy on Jerusalem”: that’s what Zechariah asked, Lord, how long will you not have mercy on Israel, “and on the cities of Judah, against which thou hast had indignation these threescore and ten years.” The seventy years was the captivity in Babylon.

“I am jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with a great jealousy. And I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease”: the heathen were at ease. “For I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction”: they helped forward the affliction upon us. All the heathen nations did that.
“Behold four horns.” “These are the horns which have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem.” The four horns are Babylon, Persia and Media, Greece, and Rome.

“And the Lord shewed me four carpenters.” The horns “scattered Judah, so that no man did lift up his head: but these”, the carpenters, “are come to fray them, to cast out the horns of the Gentiles, which lifted up their horn over the land of Judah to scatter it.”

There were carpenters in every one of those kingdoms. During Babylon you had Ezekiel and Jeremiah. During the time of Persia and Media you had Ezra, Zechariah, and Daniel, a prophet in Babylon and Persia. During the time of the Maccabees you had Judas, Simon, the five brothers. During Rome you had the apostles, John the Baptist, and Christ. Very good.

We’re still talking about the carpenters. He had a dream about this image, a man made of gold, silver and clay. Daniel told him what the dream was, and Daniel gave the interpretation of the dream.

“And as the toes of the feet were part of iron, and part of clay”: the feet is the last of the Roman Empire, and this is what we’re in right now. The ten toes represent NATO, the EU. “So the kingdom shall be partly strong”: these last kingdoms, America and NATO, are partly strong militarily. “And partly broken”: because if you have a kingdom made of all nations, each nation wants to dominate, each nation wants bills, each nation wants legislation made. You cannot please everybody.

“They shall mingle themselves with the seed of men: but they shall not cleave one to another, even as iron is not mixed with clay.” That’s why you cannot please everybody. When you have the kingdom of all nations, all nationalities, they are not going to cleave one to another.

“And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom”: the days of these kings is referring down here, to the feet, the time of America, the time of NATO. You might ask why it doesn’t start up there with Rome. Remember, all men that had life died; everybody that followed Christ was destroyed, then we went into slavery, and we started to reawaken down here in America.

The kingdom is the twelve tribes of Israel, “which shall never be destroyed.” When people ask what is the difference between true biblical Israel and those other movements, like Marcus Garvey’s group, Martin Luther King’s group, the Black Panther Party: those movements died with the men that founded them. Those men were the power. This truth, Christ the King, is the power behind us. What one man knows, all the other men know, all the other sisters know; if one falls, there’s going to be somebody else coming right behind. How many leaders are in these last days? A hundred and forty-four thousand. I don’t care how ruthless the ADL makes their legislation, it doesn’t make a difference: the Bible prophesies this will never be destroyed. No matter how many of us die, get killed or get incarcerated, the proper teachings will go on and on; it’s going to blossom. The feds ain’t going to be able to destroy nothing, the CIA ain’t going to be able to destroy nothing, the ADL ain’t going to be able to destroy nothing. Even if they make up some law, some lie, and say y’all got to come out of that building, it’s only going to make this truth go further and further.

“And the kingdom shall not be left to other people”: this is not for other races, not for other nationalities, to enjoy. That’s for all you brothers tottering on the fence, not sure if the teachings are correct. Get mad if you want, stick your lip out, I don’t care.

An Edomite woman wrote a letter. She sends her donations pretty much regularly, and her young son had been congregating for three years. Then her oldest son came back into the picture and convinced his little brother, Jesus loves everybody, it’s not right that it’s only for Israelites, that sounds racist. Now the young son has gone into the world doing whatever, and she asked what is she to do; she thought she was going to get some little crumb in the coming kingdom. To Esau, all of you: keep the commandments and the faith of Christ. We’re not allowed to tell anybody to break God’s laws. People say there was a lot of mixing going on, and that’s true. So if perchance somewhere down the line there’s a little Israelite back there on your daddy’s side, there’s nothing nobody can say or do to prevent you being saved. But if you’re not Israel, get ready for slavery.

“But it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms”: Christ is going to break in pieces NATO, break in pieces America, break in pieces Britain, all the kingdoms on the earth. This is war. “And it shall stand for ever.”

precepts.why:
“For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the strangers shall be joined with them”: the other nations are going to be joined with us. “And they shall cleave to the house of Jacob”: that means they’re going to learn the laws, statutes and commandments.

“And the house of Israel shall possess them”: we shall possess them, “in the land of the Lord for servants”, they’re going to be our servants, “and handmaids”, they’re going to be our handmaids. “And they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.”

That’s for you Israelites teetering on the side of the fence, not sure if it’s true. The other nations will be there, but they’re going to be our servants. The kingdom is not left to other people.

“But avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and contentions, and strivings about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain.” This is why Paul said to avoid genealogies: because of the great amount of mixing amongst Israel.

The movie Little White Lies, on Netflix and Amazon, shows it. The little girl was raised as Amalek. Her mom had an affair with a black man, and she didn’t know until she became an adult, but she always knew she looked a little different: that little high yellow complexion, her lips a little different, her nose a little broader. It didn’t come out until decades later. So even amongst the rug rats, Amalek, there are people that are our people. She married a black man near the end, a brother, all praise to the Lord, beautiful black children.

That’s why in our teaching we just teach. Christ said my sheep hear my voice, and strangers they will not follow. Some of them can only go back a few generations.

And in case you don’t know it, women lie. She led this whole family to believe that little high yellow girl was the product of her Edomite husband, and she held that lie until it couldn’t hold on no more. Brothers, that baby you think is yours just might not be yours. I hope I hurt nobody’s feelings. Y’all having babies now: they need to make DNA testing mandatory, but you brothers need to request it, and if she gets mad, F her, because if she’s mad she’s trying to hide something. Oh, you don’t trust me? Shut the hell up and go sit your behind down somewhere.

What if they kill the leaders? There are 144,000 leaders; all you men have to see yourselves as leaders, because that’s what you are.

“And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock”: this rock is Christ himself. “I will build my church”: he will build his church. “And the gates of hell”: the gates of hell is the CIA, FBI, ADL, SPLC and so forth and so on, “shall not prevail against it.” You hear what the Saviour said? That’s the same thing Daniel said, that it shall never be destroyed.

“The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: Which indeed is the least of all seeds”: you can see the grain of mustard seed on the fingertips; that’s how small it is, the smallest of all seeds. “But when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becometh a tree.”

Christ is explaining that’s how the kingdom of heaven is. “So that the birds of the air come”: all the nations are going to have to come and submit themselves to the Israelites. All the birds have got to come and learn. The kingdom starts small and blossoms; it shall never be destroyed.

sense.text:
The feet and toes haven’t been destroyed yet. But just like there were carpenters during the time of Babylon, Daniel and the three brothers with him; during Persia and Media, Zechariah, Ezra, the high priest Joshua, Zerubbabel, Nehemiah, a whole lot during that time; in Greece the Maccabees; in Rome Christ and the twelve apostles, and the many disciples that followed under them that you read about in the book of Acts, Barnabas and the rest of them: now here in America, down here at the feet, we in this building are about that thing right there. This is war.

“And after three days and an half”: after three hundred and fifty years of slavery and oppression, “the Spirit of life from God entered into them”, the Holy Spirit entered into us, “and they stood upon their feet”: we began to stand upon our feet as the Israelites. “And great fear fell upon them which saw them.” This is the resurrecting of the Israelites.

precepts.why: Put some names to them. “And now, brother, behold what glory; and see the people that come from the east: Unto whom I will give for leaders, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob”, and the prophets named after them through Malachi, “which is called also an angel of the Lord.” Notice it names fifteen right there. These are the leaders God gives to the people that come from the east.

“For thy help will I send my servants”: now he mentions two more prophets, Isaiah and Jeremiah, “after whose counsel I have sanctified and prepared for thee twelve trees laden with divers fruits”: these are possibly the twelve apostles right there. “And as many fountains flowing with milk and honey, and seven mighty mountains”: seven more, “whereupon there grow roses and lilies, whereby I will fill thy children with joy.”

The Lord has prophesied that he’s sending everybody back. The only thing is, nobody is going to know who is who. “There is no remembrance of former things”: Zechariah ain’t going to remember he’s Zechariah, Obadiah won’t remember he’s Obadiah, Abraham won’t remember he’s Abraham, Isaac won’t remember he’s Isaac. “Neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come.”

Our memories are wiped clean. He said you’re going back to the earth and you’re going to start again. Your name is going to be Pooky in the beginning; don’t worry about that, Pooky, you’re going to get your real name later on. So Pooky grows up, and he starts to become a prophet.

sense.text: “And after these things I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth”: the four winds represent the armies of the world, “that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree.”

“And I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God: and he cried with a loud voice to the four angels, to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea, Saying, Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” The angels are being told, don’t let the armies loose, don’t let Armageddon begin, until the servants of our God are sealed.

“And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” These are the leaders, and they’re not going to remember who they are. We have the understanding that God said I’m sending back: fifteen was the first number, in 2 Esdras 1; then the second chapter mentioned two, then twelve, then seven. You’re not going to know who none of these guys are.

That’s why it says how could you say you love God, whom you never see, but hate your brother, whom you see. You don’t know who you’re hating, so just shut your mouth and learn to love your neighbour as you love yourself. You don’t know who that brother is; just be quiet.

precepts.why: The precept for the wind. “And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea.” A multitude of men from the four winds: these are armies, these are militaries. The four winds the angels hold are the armies of the world.
Sealed with what? The …? Hell no. “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” The servants of our God are sealed with the law.

sense.text: Back to 2 Esdras 2: “And as many fountains flowing with milk and honey, and seven mighty mountains, whereupon there grow roses and lilies, whereby I will fill thy children with joy.”

“Do right to the widow, judge for the fatherless, give to the poor, defend the orphan, clothe the naked, Heal the broken and the weak”: what it’s telling us is keep the commandments, do what the Lord says to do. This plays a big part in these last days.

See the part, heal the broken. It’s as important as the word we’ve been talking about, brothers: carpenters. Carpenters are builders. We have to learn to heal the broken, broken in mind, broken in spirit. “Laugh not a lame man to scorn”, “and let the blind man come into the sight of my clearness”: show them the understanding.

“Keep the old and young within thy walls.” “Wheresoever thou findest the dead, take them and bury them, and I will give thee the first place in my resurrection.” This is why, even when our people pass, we take it very seriously.

“As for the servants whom I have given thee, there shall not one of them perish; for I will require them from among thy number.” The perish is talking about that eternal death, the eternal damnation, the lake of fire. Many of our people will physically die, but they are not going to perish in that condemnation.

So we have to start looking at death differently: death is a door to eternal life. Church Christianity taught you that death is a door to damnation. It’s only that if you’re wicked, if you’re in the midst of adultery, a fornicator, a liar, a child molester, a pedophile; then yeah, you’re going to get yours.

“Be not weary”: brothers, don’t give up; sisters, don’t give up. Some of you go through battle fatigue in this truth. A year, two years in, you get tired of the same thing: I’m reading the Bible, I’m standing on the corner, I’m getting yelled at by big mouth black women, I’m sick of this. That’s Satan; you’re getting weary. Change it up and go to the Lord in prayer and supplication. A sister that’s been with us four or five years without a man, battle fatigue comes in and she goes back to the ex; brothers too. Get down on your knees and pray and fast, and the Lord is going to bless you.

“For when the day of trouble and heaviness cometh”: that’s what y’all need to understand, the day of trouble and heaviness will come. None of us have seen no real trouble yet. Everybody’s got pretty much a decent life; I don’t care if you live in a hole in the wall, your life is better than what we see when we travel to other countries. None of y’all want to trade places with them: you’ve got working toilets here, you could get welfare; in Africa you’re on your own, and Haiti is too jacked up.

“Others shall weep and be sorrowful”: that’s why we don’t be weary, because when the day of trouble comes, others shall weep and be sorrowful, but we that believe and keep the commandments “shalt be merry and have abundance.”
“The heathen shall envy thee”: the heathen are going to envy us, “but they shall be able to do nothing against thee, saith the Lord.” They ain’t going to be able to do nothing against us.

precepts.why:
“If any man worship the beast and his image, and receive his mark”, “The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God”: if you take this white man’s philosophies, his policies, you believe in him, his sin; that’s what it’s talking about, sin. “Which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb.” They have “no rest day nor night”, “and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name.”

That is what we don’t want. That is the lake of fire, and that is the perishing the servants are kept from.

“And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth”: these are those that died, “some to everlasting life”: some people that have died physically shall be resurrected to everlasting life. That’s godhood, that’s power. “And some to shame and everlasting contempt.” That’s what Ezra said when the angel said none of them shall perish.

“And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life”: the resurrection of life is eternal life, that’s godhood. “And they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation”: that damnation is the lake of fire. So when 2 Esdras 2:26 says none of them shall perish, it’s talking about that.
“Rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets; for God hath avenged you on her.”

This is talking about America. “And in her was found the blood of prophets, and of saints, and of all that were slain upon the earth.” In America is going to be found the blood of prophets and of saints. But I thought he said none of them should perish? The perish is talking about that eternal damnation.

Talking about America again, this metaphor as a woman, drunk with “the blood of the saints”, because America is going to kill a lot of our people that believe, “and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus.” They’re going to physically die, but they’re not going to perish in that condemnation.

sense.text: Watch what Nehemiah says about being a carpenter. “Ye see the distress that we are in, how Jerusalem lieth waste, and the gates thereof are burned with fire: come, and let us build up the wall of Jerusalem, that we be no more a reproach.”

“And they said, Let us rise up and build.” See the men Nehemiah had around him: they all agreed, they said let us rise up and build. They were carpenters. This is literal, but it also goes in the metaphorical context: a builder means a learned man. “So they strengthened their hands for this good work.”

When the enemies heard it, they laughed and “despised us, and said, What is this thing that ye do? will ye rebel against the king?” Nehemiah answered: “The God of heaven, he will prosper us; therefore we his servants will arise and build: but ye have no portion, nor right, nor memorial, in Jerusalem.” That’s what a master builder does.

“For as the master builder of a new house must care for the whole building; but he that undertaketh to set it out, and paint it, must seek out fit things for the adorning thereof: even so I think it is with us.” The writer is saying that we are that master builder. They were building a temple and putting things in it, the same way you do when you get a new house. That’s how it is in God’s truth: we build one another, we got to bring things in.

“Did ye never read in the scriptures, The stone which the builders rejected”. Another word for builders is carpenters. The builders, the carpenters in his time that he was making reference to, were those religious leaders: the Pharisees, the scribes, the Sanhedrin, the Levites, that high priesthood.

“The same is become the head of the corner”: the same is become the master, the leader. “This is the Lord’s doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes.”

Think about it: you’re going to build a house and you see a huge, strong stone. Somebody says that would be the best stone to be the foundation of the house, and they say no, we want that stone back there, because my friend gave me that stone. The stone that they rejected was Christ. But the Lord said, regardless of what they choose, I have still chosen Christ as the chief cornerstone, the king, the leader.

precepts.why:
“This is the stone which was set at nought of you builders, which is become the head of the corner.” He still became the head of the corner.

That goes to show you: brothers often say ‘I’ve been overlooked in the congregation.’ Brother, don’t worry, God sees everything that you do. Christ was overlooked by the religious leaders, and God said I still chose him; his works and his teachings superseded everybody. Let your work speak for you. Ain’t got no works? You probably ain’t got no damn works, and that’s why you’re overlooked. If the works is there, show me your faith and the works is going to be there; faith without works is dead.

Brothers that make noise wherever they go want to be put in a position, getting it through an unworthy way: ‘I’m gonna be around Bishop so he’ll put me there.’ Nobody is going to put you nowhere that way. Everybody gets asked, what do you think about this brother, what do you think about that brother, and once everybody says no, then it’s no.

sense.text:
Watch the building the carpenters did after Christ resurrected and went on high. “After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David”: the 12 tribes of Israel, “which is fallen down”. He is quoting Amos.

That lets you know that carpenters had to be resurrected. In order to build you need builders, you need carpenters: new carpenters, new builders. The same thing then is the same thing now. “And I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up”: God will set it up. That’s what we read in Daniel 2, a kingdom which shall never be destroyed.

“That the residue of men might seek after the Lord”: the residue of men, as Esau. How are they going to seek after the Lord? In captivity, because we are going to possess them. “And all the Gentiles”: Jews and Christians, “upon whom my name is called”. They say, I’m Jewish, I am Christian. “Saith the Lord, who doeth all these things.”

This is saying the same thing Amos 9:12 is saying; Peter just used different wording. Acts is saying the same thing Amos is saying.

precepts.why:
Amos prophesied it; the apostles lived it. “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof”: bring them together, unify them, unite them in solidarity. “And I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old”: the 12 tribes of Israel built as in the days of old.

“That they may possess the remnant of Edom”: we may possess the remnant of Edom, “and of all the heathen, which are called by my name”, the Jews and Christians. We are going to possess all of them. That is the residue of men and the Gentiles of Acts 15:17.

sense.text:
We’re builders, brothers. Sisters, y’all got some kids: you are builders too. You’re supposed to deal with their minds in their first stages of life. You put the wrong thing in children, they grow up all confused, and that’s a negro word, confused.

“As a wise masterbuilder”: what was the apostle Paul? A wise master builder. What must we become? A wise master builder. We have to be just like that. That’s why when brothers say ‘I reject the apostle Paul’, ignore them; if y’all ain’t like that, you’re going to be confused. A lot of these single sisters online watch all these Israelite camps: ‘we don’t deal with Paul’, ‘neither do we deal with Luke’, ‘we reject 1 John’, ‘we reject 2 Peter’. You keep watching them videos and then you come in, ‘I’m confused’, because you stupid: you reject the scriptures. When you hear people say John the Baptist was fake, he had a fake Israelite camp, reject that. Those are not wise master builders. All we can do is warn y’all, and when you come in here with stupidity, security throws that out.

A sister in one of the schools was up there with them brothers that hate us. We don’t hate them; they hate us and speak evil about us. She’s not with us; she got to go. Single sister, I pray for you, because a lot of you don’t got your heads on right: you got no guidance, you have no hedge, you’re all over the place.

“I have laid the foundation, and another buildeth thereon”. We go to different places and teach, and I can’t be everywhere. So we send other brothers, younger men coming up: go there and water this truth. There’s a congregation in this country, go over there, follow up with them, see what’s going on, teach them, guide them. We go and we lay the foundation, and we send brother captains and officers behind us to build thereon. It’s nothing new that we’re doing.

“But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon.” That’s the thing.

“For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.” We can never ignore the chief cornerstone. When we see brothers tend to lean to one side and ignore Christ the King, you’re going to have to go. Christ is the King, he’s the Lord of lords, he is the Alpha and Omega.
“Now if any man build upon this foundation gold”: we want to build gold. “Silver”: we want to build silver. “Precious stones”: we want to build precious stones. Then “wood, hay, stubble.”

“Every man’s work shall be made manifest: for the day shall declare it, because it shall be revealed by fire; and the fire shall try every man’s work of what sort it is.” When we send brothers out, we’re trusting them to build men and women the best they can. Your goal is to build them to the gold, the silver, the precious stones. But if you go there and lollygag, do a half stepping job, and come out with wood, hay and stubble, your work is going to come out; it’s going to be revealed.

We send brothers out and they find people that are weak as hell: murmurers, complainers, adulterers, liars. Is nobody teaching properly out here? This is why the internet is very important, downloading the videos is very important, and traveling is very important, because we know a day is going to come when they shut this down, all the videos we got.

precepts.why:
“And are built upon the foundation of the apostles”. What was Paul? A wise master builder. When you hear brothers say ‘we reject the apostle Paul, we reject the apostle Peter’, those are not wise master builders.

“And prophets”: when you hear brothers say ‘we don’t go by the Old Testament prophets, we reject their teaching’, they’re not wise master builders either. “Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”: when you hear brothers say ‘we don’t deal with what they call JC’, they are not wise master builders.

“In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord”: we’re the temple, brothers and sisters, we’re growing in his truth. “In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit”: all of us are builded together on that foundation that Paul laid as a wise master builder.

Not only do they reject Paul, they reject John the Baptist. Here is what Christ said about John: “But what went ye out for to see? A prophet? yea, I say unto you, and more than a prophet.” Jesus Christ the King, the Lord of lords, our creator, said he’s more than a prophet. Don’t look strange because Christ is called our creator: John 1 says he created all things, and there was nothing made without him.

“For this is he, of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.” Christ says what Malachi prophesied about in Malachi 3:1 was about John.

“Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he”, because in the kingdom we are all going to be righteous, sinless. Christ said there’s nobody greater than John born of women. How are you going to read that and say John was wicked, that he made a wicked Israelite camp? Those are not wise master builders. All we can do is warn you. You single sisters looking for love in all the wrong places, you going to get yours.

sense.text: “Unto you therefore which believe he is precious”: Christ is precious. “But unto them which be disobedient”, disobedient to the teachings of Christ, “the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner”.

“And a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence”: Christ has become a rock of offence to brothers and sisters that reject his teachings. “Even to them which stumble at the word, being disobedient”. Why do you stumble at the word? Because you are an adulterer, because you are a liar, because you are a thief. That’s why you stumble at the word.

“Whereunto also they were appointed.” Some of you were appointed like that, appointed to be fornicators, liars, thieves, whatever. You have to shake yourself out of that; you better go before the Lord. And if your bottom lip is stuck out, that’s because you’re guilty.

“And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places”: our people shall build. “Thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations”: we shall raise up the foundations of many generations. “And thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach”: that’s what we’re going to be called in the kingdom, the repairers of the breach, carpenters, builders. “The restorer of paths to dwell in”: we all shall be called the restorer of paths to dwell in.

We give you men and women the tools; we give you the scriptures; we give you the precepts. “But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith”: as a master builder, the first thing you must build is yourself. We can’t do it for you; all we can do is give you the scriptures. When y’all sit with us or around us, you apply, but it’s your alone time that shows your integrity, that shows if you truly believe what you are reading.

As master builders, all of us becoming master builders and repairers of the breach, we have to learn to be free of the works of the flesh.

The ad department made an ad that said, ‘we are a peaceful people, but the God we serve is not.’ Somebody is saying, doesn’t the Bible call him the Prince of Peace? Yeah, he’s the Prince of Peace to the 12 tribes of Israel that obey.

“If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.” We are commanded to be a peaceful people: not in rioting, not in gathering weapons to cause civil unrest.

precepts.why: “Follow peace with all men, and holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord”. See what the Bible says: follow peace with all men. We are a peaceful people; the Bible teaches us to be peaceful. But to be peaceful don’t mean don’t teach. Our job is to teach.

sense.text:
Christ says it: “And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.” This is the test for whether you are an Edomite or not. When we go over these scriptures on Esau, we see where your heart and your mind is. If you ain’t Esau, it ain’t going to offend you.

A lot of our brothers we meet from Puerto Rico and other places, some of them mixed, we tell them: we are going to go through the scriptures, and if you are mad at what God said he is going to do to Esau, this ain’t for you. That goes for the dark skinned too: some of you got a Negro mentality, and if you get mad at what God says, this ain’t for you. Blessed is he whosoever is not offended.

We are peaceful people; the Bible says be at peace with all men. “Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord”: the land of the north is North America. “For I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven.”
“Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” The daughter of Babylon is Edom. We are dwelling with the daughter of Babylon here, so we dwell here now.

We are peaceful people, but God is not. “For thus saith the Lord of hosts; After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you”: the nations that spoiled Israel. “For he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.” He that touches the Israelites touches his lover. We are God’s fervent love, we are his bride.

So when the nations touch us there is no peace. There ain’t no love there. They destroyed his people, and he said, no, I’m not letting you get away with that.

There are necessary steps all of us got to take to be counted worthy in God’s good graces in this coming Kingdom, and here is one of the steps we must have: “But without faith it is impossible to please him.” If you don’t have faith that these words are true, you cannot please God. Faith is paramount; that is what the Lord is requiring of us.

precepts.why: “And every one that shall be saved”: and everybody wants to be saved when this coming destruction comes. “And shall be able to escape by his works”: the works is keeping the commandments. “And by faith”: for without faith it is impossible to please God. Works and faith, “whereby ye have believed.” To escape, it takes both.

“Therefore we are always confident, knowing that, whilst we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord.” That is another understanding of death: while we are home in this body we are absent from the Lord.

“For we walk by faith, not by sight”: go by what the Bible says.

“We are confident, I say, and willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord.” Paul is letting us know that once we are out of this body we are in the Lord’s presence. Paul understood death, that’s why he didn’t fear it. Peter understood death, that’s why he didn’t fear it. The prophets understood death, that’s why they didn’t fear it. We’ve never understood death, that’s why we fear, but we are learning now.

“Wherefore we labour”: we work in this truth, “that, whether present or absent, we may be accepted of him.” The bottom line is we want the Lord to accept us, whether we are here in this body and definitely when we are out of this body. We want to hear, well done thou good and faithful servant.

sense.text: “But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God”: the righteous never dies. “And there shall no torment touch them”: that is the same torment we read earlier, the lake of fire, the second death. That is not going to touch us.

“In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die”: the unwise is the ADL. We seem to die because our body dies; our bodies perish. “And their departure is taken for misery”: oh, you had a miserable life, all you did was read that Bible and teach that Bible, you had a miserable life and now you’re dead. That’s what it means.
“And their going from us to be utter destruction”: whether you are shot, stabbed, however it goes down. “But they are in peace”: the righteous are at peace.

“For though they be punished in the sight of men”: through incarceration, through torment, whether we get shot, stabbed, beheaded, whatever it is. One of the apostles was beat down by a group of people with clubs. That’s a terrible death, a long death. That ain’t like getting beheaded, where you die quick; getting beat with sticks takes some time, that’s pain.

“Yet is their hope full of immortality”: they are in godhood, they are immortal.

“And having been a little chastised”: the clubbing you got, the shooting, the beheading, they burned you to death, they drowned you, they tied you up in the back of a car and dragged your body down the street. God says that’s a little chastised. No matter what form of death we go through, whether it’s sickness and pain or not, it is a little chastisement. That is what we are going to go through in these last days: no matter what the torment, torture or incarceration period is, God calls it a little chastised.

“They shall be greatly rewarded”: we’re going to get eternal life, salvation, godhood. There’s no comparison between the godhood and immortality we shall get and the chastisement we suffer. That’s what King Solomon is telling us.

“For God proved them, and found them worthy for himself”: that’s the point right there. The Lord said, I’m going to test you, I’m going to try you, I’m going to prove you. God proved us, he tested us, and the ones he found worthy are those that confessed him before men that were putting them to death.

“As gold in the furnace hath he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.” The death of the saints is like a burnt offering, and God loves that smell. That’s some heavy stuff. Christ fulfilled the law of sacrifice, and our death is doing the same thing: that’s the sacrifice I’m looking for, he said.

“And in the time of their visitation they shall shine”: we shall shine. That means we are going to get that eternal life, that godhood, that new body. “And run to and fro like sparks among the stubble”: that’s power, supernatural power. The stubble is the nations.

“They shall judge the nations”: we are going to judge the nations, rule the nations, dominate the nations, “and have dominion over the people.” “And their Lord shall reign for ever”: Christ shall reign forever.

precepts.why:
God proved them and found them worthy for himself; here is how he proves us. “Fear them not therefore: for there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known.”

“What I tell you in darkness”: all those parables, those mysteries, “that speak ye in light”. Christ says, I want you to break it down publicly for the world to hear it. “And what ye hear in the ear”: that is the parables, the mysteries, the understandings, “that preach ye upon the housetops”. Preach it loud for everybody to hear it.

Understand this: what you preach that I’ve told you in secret is going to get you killed. The mysteries and the teachings I’ve given you will get you killed. “And fear not them which kill the body”: your body will be killed, “but are not able to kill the soul”. They can’t touch the real you, your soul. “But rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.” You better fear God. You worried about that little flimsy body you got, that weak broke down body? It got an expiration date on it. What you scared for?

“Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father.” A bird won’t drop dead without God saying it’s time for that bird to die, and he is talking about us: nobody in here dies, nobody listening dies, until the Father says now it’s time. “But the very hairs of your head are all numbered”: that’s how important you are. “Fear ye not therefore, ye are of more value than many sparrows”: you are more important than a bird.

“Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men”: confess me in what context? Fear of death, because that’s what he was talking about, don’t fear them that kill the body. “Him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.” When you are at the point of being put to death, if you confess me before men I will confess you. “But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven”: if you deny me when you’re about to die, I’m going to deny you.

The brother or sister that is afraid of death proves they don’t have faith. If you believe the scripture read earlier, that when you leave this body you are going to be with Christ, you are not going to be afraid of death. The reason you are afraid is because you don’t believe what this Bible says. The bunny hoppers don’t believe nothing.

So those God proved and found worthy in Wisdom of Solomon 3:5 are those that confessed him before men that were putting them to death.

“They shall shine” in Wisdom of Solomon is the same thing Daniel 12:3 said. “And they that be wise”: those that keep the commandments, “shall shine as the brightness of the firmament”. That’s godhood, another level: the immortality, the celestial body we seek for. “And they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.”

sense.text:
This is saying the same thing as Wisdom of Solomon 3, that the righteous shall judge the nations and have dominion over the people. “And he that overcometh”: overcome what? The works of the flesh. We all are battling with something, and it’s up to us to identify it, take moral inventory where we fall short, what we are struggling with. Some of y’all, soon as you get a body here, you smoking a blunt.

“And keepeth my works unto the end”: you got to keep God’s commandments until the end. “To him will I give power over the nations”: that’s what we read in Daniel 12:3 and in Wisdom of Solomon 3:1-8.

“And he shall rule them”: we are going to rule the nations, “with a rod of iron”. We ain’t going to play with the other nations; we are going to teach them God’s laws. “As the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers”: we are going to break the nations to pieces to teach them God’s laws. It ain’t no ‘oh, I’m sorry, let me get it right’: you want to eat snake, off with your head; you want to be a pedophile, off with your head.

“Even as I received of my Father”: Christ received that gift of his Father, and he said, I’m giving it to you, Israelites.
“And I will give him the morning star”: he is going to give us understanding like we could not believe. That’s why we say godhood.

precepts.why:
He that overcometh must overcome the works of the flesh. “Now the works of the flesh are manifest”: all of us in here and all of us watching online must do a moral inventory of ourselves, a self-examination regarding the works of the flesh.

“Adultery”: if you are an adulterer, you know you are battling with the works of the flesh right there. “Fornication”: fornication covers a lot of stuff; it deals with incest too, and with dealing with a woman on her menstrual cycle. “Uncleanness”: vile affection, for you pedophiles. Don’t say none of you are pedophiles: we had a brother in North Carolina who was the first one to say the school is too far, but the Negro drove four hours to meet a 13 year old girl and met Chris Hansen. We ain’t bailing you and we ain’t helping you. “Lasciviousness”: offensive sexual desires. Pedophilia deals with that, homosexuality deals with that, you lesbians out there.

“Idolatry”: idolatry covers a lot, whatever you put before God. It could be money; some of you women are only after money, how much money he got, he got benefits, he got a job. “Witchcraft”: if you deal with horoscopes, the zodiac, the sun, the moon and the stars and what the alignments are, you are dealing with witchcraft. Weed is witchcraft, that’s right, I said it: if you smoke weed to get a high you are dealing with witchcraft. Brother can’t rap until he smoke weed. “Hatred”: some of you deal with hatred up in here. “Variance”: you always got to be conflicting; I say A, you say B. “Emulations”: when you like to imitate in a negative context, I could do what you do and I do it better. “Wrath”: you’re always angry. “Strife”: anytime you come around there’s a strife spirit, an argument. “Seditions” and “heresies”: you come with another doctrine.

“Envyings”: you are jealous of what he got or she got. “Murders”: you want to put people to death; that deals with malice. “Drunkenness”: you don’t know your limit, you drink too much. “Revellings”: you love to party.

sense.text:
We want that godhood, but will we receive opposition? Yes, we will. “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.”

The four horns we read earlier are Babylon, Media-Persia, the Greeks and Rome. The things written aforetime show that our people received opposition under every one of them while trying to keep the commandments: in Babylon, in Media-Persia, in Greece and in the early stages of Rome. Esau has always done that, and it is written for our learning, because we will receive it today.

precepts.why:
When our people were in Babylon trying to keep the commandments, did they receive opposition? “Wherefore at that time certain Chaldeans came near, and accused the Jews”: they accused us.

They said to Nebuchadnezzar, King, live forever, no disrespect, you made a law that whoever hears the music has got to bow to the statue, has got to bow to the idol, “And whoso falleth not down and worshippeth, that he should be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace.”

“There are certain Jews whom thou hast set over the affairs of the province of Babylon, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego; these men, O king, have not regarded thee”: they have disrespected the king. “They serve not thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.” That’s called opposition. It was a set up. That is the example from Babylon.

During the time of Persia-Media we got opposition too. “When Sanballat heard that we builded the wall, he was wroth, and took great indignation, and mocked the Jews.” He said, “What do these feeble Jews? will they fortify themselves? will they sacrifice? will they make an end in a day?” And Tobiah the Ammonite said, “Even that which they build, if a fox go up, he shall even break down their stone wall.”

Nehemiah prayed against the enemies: “Hear, O our God; for we are despised: and turn their reproach upon their own head”, “And cover not their iniquity, and let not their sin be blotted out from before thee: for they have provoked thee to anger before the builders.”

“So built we the wall; and all the wall was joined together unto the half thereof: for the people had a mind to work.” Notice that. The people we need around us must have a mind to work. If you got brothers and sisters who have been in a congregation and have no works in the body, they are wasting our time. Not the old, the sick and the ailing, but young able men and young able sisters who just sit there and do nothing in the body. You want to hear gossip, they got gossip for you. They are a waste of time; they don’t have a mind to work.

When Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabians, the Ammonites and the Ashdodites heard “that the walls of Jerusalem were made up, and that the breaches began to be stopped, then they were very wroth”: they were pissed when the Israelites organized themselves and did God’s work. “And conspired all of them together to come and to fight against Jerusalem, and to hinder it.” All the nations conspired against our forefathers. That is the opposition we got in Persia-Media.

Now the Greeks. “Neither was it lawful for a man to keep sabbath days”, “or to profess himself at all to be a Jew.” The Greeks made laws against God’s laws: new legislation which opposed the Most High’s commandments, and legislation making it illegal for us to call ourselves the Israelites. You think it could never happen now in these last days; you have no idea.

The Jews were brought “by bitter constraint to eat of the sacrifices”, and “compelled to go in procession to Bacchus, carrying ivy.”

“Moreover there went out a decree”: listen good to this decree, these laws, “to the neighbour cities of the heathen”, “against the Jews”, against our fathers, “that they should observe the same fashions, and be partakers of their sacrifices”. They made a law saying you got to follow the same customs as the Greeks. “And whoso would not conform themselves to the manners of the Gentiles should be put to death. Then might a man have seen the present misery.”

What about Rome? Acts 12 is the early stages of the Roman Empire. “Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church.” Herod the king was an Edomite; he would be part of the ADL today. He stretched forth his hand to vex certain of the Israelites.

“And he killed James the brother of John with the sword”: he cut his head off. “And because he saw it pleased the Jews”: it pleased the wicked Israelites, “he proceeded further to take Peter also”: he arrested Peter.

He put him in prison “intending after Easter”, the pagan holiday Easter which we never celebrated, “to bring him forth to the people.” They wanted to kill Peter publicly in front of everybody, to make a big show, like at the end of Braveheart when they made his execution public, or like in The Birth of a Nation about Nat Turner: they killed him publicly to put fear in all the slaves. Esau has always done that.

sense.text:
We read the opposition during the time of Babylon, Persia-Media, the Greeks and the early stages of Rome; what about today? This is a parable. The dragon in this parable is the white man; America, that’s them, that’s the dragon. The serpent is the dragon.

“And the serpent cast out of his mouth water as a flood”: the waters is their lies, their communication. CNN, New York Times, 21st Century Fox, NBC, CBS, NPR, and the list goes on and on. It’s all them; it has always been them. “After the woman”: we’re the woman, we’re the bride of Christ, “that he might cause her to be carried away of the flood.”

“And the earth helped the woman”: the earth is those men, those prophets, those apostles resurrected, helping Israel and guiding Israel. The earth don’t just jump up and help you. We are made from the earth. You need men, you need women to go out and help build, help teach, help guide, help lead.

“And the earth opened her mouth”: the way we open our mouth is with this Bible, in teaching. The Bible does not speak by itself; it needs prophets, it needs apostles, it needs teachers. “And swallowed up the flood which the dragon cast out of his mouth.”

“And the dragon was wroth with the woman”: the dragon is going to get so angry, “and went to make war”. This war is physical, no more words. They say, let’s make laws, let’s make legislation to arrest them for hate speech, for saying that they’re the Jews and we’re not; oh, that’s hate speech, it’s going to lead to another Holocaust. Go to Congress and make laws and get them arrested, and while they’re arrested torture them, get them fired from their jobs, have them lose their houses, their homes, their jobs, break up their families.

“With the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ”: that’s you and me. Understand this is war. It’s been talked of for a long time, but they’re already making laws; that is in the book about the Jewish onslaught. Now they’re going to create a scenario. They thought they had us with that Jersey shooting, but it didn’t work: they couldn’t prove it was any Israelite camp, the liars that they are. They are going to come up with something, maybe somebody sitting among us doing something evil and stupid, and say, look what the Israelites did.

precepts.why:
There are many precepts regarding the earth, and this is one. “But we have this treasure in earthen vessels”: the treasure we have is the knowledge, the wisdom, the understanding, and these earthen vessels are our bodies, “that the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us.” It is all of God and not of us.

So the earth that helps the woman is men: the earthen vessels carrying that treasure, the prophets and apostles who help, guide and teach Israel.

sense.text:
When they shut the teaching down we’re going to go out two by twos; we’re going to cover the face of every city, the face of every country we can. Ain’t no fear, brothers. And you scary cats, go home, we don’t need you scary cat brothers or sisters, to hell with you.

“The wicked plotteth against the just”, “and gnasheth upon him with his teeth.” That FBI director was asked what was the single greatest threat to the USA, and he answered negro unity. That’s the FBI; they got buildings and streets named after him, and they still believe in that policy, that philosophy, that negro unity is a threat to the United States of America. Why? What do they know that the churches don’t know? Our unity is the resurrection of the twelve tribes of Israel.

precepts.why: See what David said: “Hide me from the secret counsel of the wicked”, “from the insurrection of the workers of iniquity”. They are plotting behind the scenes, making laws, rules, regulations. Y’all see what they’re doing in Palestine. You think it can never happen here? How wrong you are, how wrong you are.

These are the people that run the world. “So shall they fear the name of the Lord from the west”: we live in the western hemisphere. “And his glory from the rising of the sun”: that’s why our brothers and sisters are in the eastern hemisphere.

“When the enemy shall come in like a flood”: when the enemy comes against us like we read in Revelation 12:15-17, “the Spirit of the Lord shall lift up a standard against him.” He’s only going to allow them to do but so much, he’s only going to allow the wicked to do but so much. Why? To test us, to prove us. That’s what Christ was saying in Matthew 10: fear not them that kill the body. It’s going to be a test.

“And the Redeemer shall come to Zion, and unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob, saith the Lord.” That’s what the Lord is looking for, that’s what our Redeemer is looking for: those men and women that keep the commandments. Prove yourself, brothers and sisters, prove yourself.

sense.text:
Victory over sin can never be won without struggle. You must struggle first to attain the victory.

“For whatsoever is born of God”: meaning born again, “overcometh the world”. You overcome the world, you overcome the sins of the world. “And this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith.” For without faith it is impossible to please God.

“For if I build again the things which I destroyed”: put that tree back up, put the works of the flesh back up. When we’re born again and come into this truth we destroy the adultery we may have committed. Some of us may have been in fornication, uncleanness, revellings; some of us love the party, idolatry, witchcraft. We destroyed that and said no, I want to change my life. But if you build again the things which you destroyed, you find yourself in adultery again, fornication again, vile affection again, idolatry again, witchcraft again, filled with hate again, heresy again, murders again, drunkenness again.

“I make myself a transgressor.” Who do you make a transgressor, brothers? You make yourself one. You can’t blame nobody else: oh it’s his fault, it’s her fault, he did this to me, he said that to me. No, it’s you. You make yourself a transgressor; you did that, you chose that.

“For the wages of sin is death”: we read that in Galatians 5:19, all the works of the flesh; the wages of sin is death. And it ain’t talking about regular death. That death is not the death that everybody goes through, that this flesh goes through; it is the damnation Christ mentioned in John 5:29. The wages of breaking God’s law is damnation, condemnation. It’s not oh I had a heart attack and I die; it ain’t talking about that.

“But the gift of God is eternal life”: eternal life is immortality, celestial immortal power on the earth, “through Jesus Christ our Lord.” That’s what we all want, that’s what we all fighting for right there.

precepts.why: How do we know it ain’t talking about regular death? “Great travail is created for every man”: every man goes through tribulation, “and an heavy yoke is upon the sons of Adam, from the day that they go out of their mother’s womb, till the day that they return to the mother of all things.” The mother of all things is the earth: till the day they die.

Brothers, sisters, do you hear what the Lord said? “Fear not the sentence of death, remember them that have been before thee, and that come after; for this is the sentence of the Lord over all flesh.” All flesh dies. Death is appointed to all flesh, so that is not the death of Romans 6:23.

“And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation.” That damnation is the death Paul was talking about in Romans 6:23.

The verse above it: “Marvel not at this: for the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice”. Everybody that’s dead shall hear his voice; death is appointed to all flesh. But notice what he says in 29: they that have done good unto the resurrection of life, that’s the eternal life we just read about, and they that have done evil unto the resurrection of damnation, that’s the death in Romans 6. Now we know what kind of death he’s talking about.

sense.text: Pay close attention to this: there’s going to be a remnant of brothers, a remnant of sisters that are alive when tribulation comes. “For now are the plagues come upon the whole earth and ye shall remain in them: for God shall not deliver you, because ye have sinned against him.” Y’all see that? Because you have sinned against him.

“Surely he knoweth your inventions, and what ye think in your hearts, even them that sin, and would hide their sin.” Some of you are very good at hiding your sin. You can get past me, you can get past the deacons, get past all of us, but you’ll never get past God. That’s what he’s saying.

Some of you have been plowing out stupid women for years, in IUIC. You were with her for years, she ain’t say nothing, you didn’t say nothing, until the next perky breasted sister walked in and you happened to look at her. Then she got mad and revealed you. We asked, brother, are you sleeping with sister so and so? No brother, no, strong in the Lord and the power of his might. Really? Step outside, sister come back in here: he said you a liar. She said, oh, I got receipts; she had photographs. Why would you have photographs of the brother? She was waiting, she knew this day would come. So sister, you let him dog you out for years, you was with it and you didn’t say nothing. Stop the tears, stop the BS: you wicked, he wicked too, both of y’all wicked.

Here’s another one. A brother says he’s going on the cruise, see y’all in two weeks, and told nobody what kind of cruise. Find out the name of the boat, put it on the screen, and it was the gay love boat. You can’t make this stuff up. He knoweth your inventions and what ye think in your hearts.

“Therefore hath the Lord exactly searched out all your works”: that’s why I went over early about doing moral inventory on yourself, self-examination. That goes for all of us, because once you do it, the Lord’s already done it. “And he will put you all to shame.” He said, you know what, he or she think they got away with this; I’m going to create a scenario where it’s going to come out.

Here’s another one. Two brothers come up; one brother says I’m battling with porn, and the brother standing there curses him out: you weak, you simple, go sit yourself down. I didn’t say a word. Then that same brother says, you seen the trailer for the new movie? Let me show you. He gives me his cell phone, and whatever he looked at last pops up on the feed: Japanese anime porn. Didn’t you just curse that brother out back there? You cursed him out like a dog and you doing the same damn thing. How you feel now? You going sit your black behind down somewhere.
“And when your sins are brought forth, ye shall be ashamed before men, and your own sins shall be your accusers in that day.”

“What will ye do? or how will ye hide your sins before God and his angels? Behold, God himself is the judge, fear him”. What can we as men do to you? Nothing. We put y’all out for three weeks, a month, a couple months: I’m going go murder somebody, God forbid, bring me back in three months, y’all are good. But God himself is the judge. Fear him.

“Leave off from your sins, and forget your iniquities, to meddle no more with them for ever”. “So shall God lead you forth, and deliver you from all trouble.” We all want to be delivered from all trouble; he said don’t meddle in your sins no more.

Our goal, our ultimate goal, is the coming kingdom on earth. We want this coming kingdom. “Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth”: in where? In earth. So it ain’t going to be up in the sky, brothers. I don’t know how Christians know the Lord’s Prayer but they still say yeah we going to live up in the sky. You ain’t living up in the sky. “As it is in heaven”.

precepts.why:
I was watching this Edomite who said when Christ comes back he’s going to set the Democrats and the Republicans in order and put Britain and America as the ruling nations.

“For in the place wherein the Highest beginneth to shew his city, there can no man’s building be able to stand.” Y’all hear that? When the kingdom begins to come, no man’s building will be able to stand. There will be no Haiti, no Jamaica, none of that; it’s going to be gone. No White House. There will be no Ghana, no Congo, no Santo Domingo, no France.

“Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it”. That’s why we must always maintain to be in spirit; we want the Holy Spirit to operate through us. We want to be of the Lord; we want to be that kingdom Daniel prophesied in Daniel 2:44 that will never be destroyed. We want to be part of that.

sense.text: “But unto the wicked God saith”: this is the white man. “What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” They take the covenant of God as Jews and Christians: one takes the old covenant, one takes the new covenant.
“Seeing thou hatest instruction”: they hate God’s laws. “And castest my words behind thee”: both groups, Jews and Christians, cast God’s words behind them.

“When thou sawest a thief, then thou consentedst with him”. There was a time when you wouldn’t really understand that too much, but look on the news and you see them in Palestine stealing homes and houses that don’t belong to them. “And hast been partaker with adulterers”: that’s what them tunnels was for, adultery; that’s what them tunnels is for here in Brooklyn.
“Thou givest thy mouth to evil”: they give their mouth to speak evil, “and thy tongue frameth deceit”: they frame lies.
“Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother”: they speak against the Israelites, the real Israelites. “Thou slanderest thine own mother’s son”: they slander us.

“These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself”: they say surely Hashem is a white man, surely God Jehovah is a white man. Wrong, wrong. “But I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.” God said I will reprove you, and he will set the true Israelites in order before their eyes. That’s what you’re seeing right now; we’re living that right now, and we don’t want to be castaways.

“Wherefore the rather, brethren, give diligence”. Brothers, you feel that battle fatigue? The Bible says give diligence. How many of you ever been in a fist fight? You get tired, but you know if you give up you done. That’s how this truth is. You hope somebody break it up, but if nobody does and you give up, you getting stomped out, your teeth on the curb. Damn, nobody want to go through that. I don’t care how much battle fatigue: give diligence.

“To make your calling and election sure: for if ye do these things”: if you obey that, “ye shall never fall.”

precepts.why:
We all go through battle fatigue, brothers, but keep pushing: this is war. Remember the coward in Saving Private Ryan: he saw his partner being put to death by the German pushing a knife into him, and he was so scared to fight he just watched. Then the German gets up, sees the coward, and walks right by him: you ain’t even worth killing, you ain’t even worth a bullet. That might be some of you. You can’t go to war with me; stay home and watch the babies.

“I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem”: brothers, we are the watchmen for the nation of Israel. “Which shall never hold their peace”: that’s to give diligence to make your calling and election sure. “Day nor night”. “Ye that make mention of the Lord”: if you’re going to make mention of the Lord, “keep not silence”. Don’t keep silence: keep teaching, keep teaching, keep teaching. But I’m tired? Keep teaching.
